title: Canva Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Billing Options
summary: Canva pricing varies by seat count, monthly versus annual billing, and whether you need AI features. Know your total cost before committing.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Canva limits that explain the gap


The gap came from three places. They were who counts as a billable seat, how far AI generation stretches each month, which brand controls sit only on paid tiers, and what a plan ending does to your files.


Your headcount isn't your seat count. Anyone given a paid role is a cost, so a part-time contractor or a reviewer who only comments can change the total. **Check the member list against roles before renewal, because the invoice will count whatever the list says.**


A recurring seat check is cheap to automate.


Activepieces bills a flow run as 1 credit however many steps it contains, so a scheduled flow that posts the renewal date and seat count to Slack costs one credit a run, and the Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so on those a longer version of the same flow costs more.


### Canva AI credits and monthly generation limits


Smaller than most buyers assume, **the AI allowance is a monthly ceiling** . According to[Brand Tools Lab](https://brandtoolslab.com/tasks/ai-images/) , Pro allows 200 Premium and 20 Ultra AI uses a month.


On Business and Enterprise, both allow 400 and 40, according to Brand Tools Lab. That means a team generating image variants for a campaign can exhaust Pro's 20 Ultra uses within days.


**Business doubles the room but still ends** , so moving up a tier doesn't remove the cap.


### Canva brand controls on paid plans


Without locked templates, approved colors and fonts, and similar guardrails, a ten-person team stops looking like one company. If your plan lacks them, the cost shows up as inconsistent output and rework, and you pay it in staff hours, not on the invoice.


List the controls you rely on and confirm each is in the tier you're buying.


When you downgrade or cancel, you can be left with files you can open but not fully use, such as paid-only assets or brand settings that no longer apply.


Export what you need and test a downgrade on one project first. Finding out at the deadline costs far more than checking now.
